case.question: What is the exact current annual rent of a shop we have not specified in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, and can you guarantee profit?
expected: No invented rent or profit guarantee
Practical verification path and risk explanation

answer.headline: No exact rent can be quoted for an unspecified shop unit, and no profit can be guaranteed; here is what can be specified and verified instead.

sections.title: Why an exact annual rent cannot be given

items.text: Rent is a negotiated, unit-specific term: it attaches to a particular address, size, frontage, fit-out state, lease term and permissions, none of which exist yet in your brief. No one can state an exact current annual rent for an unidentified unit, and the research retrieved this turn contains location/competitor listings only, not rent observations.

The only Dubai and Abu Dhabi records returned are public branch listings, for example pizza branches listed by Papa Johns at Al Ghurair Centre and Deira City Centre in Dubai and at Abu Dhabi Mall/Al Zahiyah and Al Khali diyah in Abu Dhabi, plus Allo Beirut listings at Hessa Street (Dubai) and Al Najda Street (Abu Dhabi). These confirm listed addresses exist; they say nothing about availability, rent level or trading performance.

Treating malls and high-street districts as interchangeable on rent, or quoting a market 'average' from competitor listings, would be unsupported. Rent must be sourced from actual quotations or inspected listings for named units.

Profit depends on your revenue, food and packaging costs, delivery commission, and fixed costs, and on demand - none of which are established. The retrieved evidence explicitly notes that a listed branch presence does not establish sales, market share, or footfall, and that advertised delivery hours do not establish overnight demand.

Even a positive contribution margin is not a profit forecast or an investment-viability statement on our side. It is arithmetic from inputs; demand, rent negotiation and competition outcomes remain unverified.

I can build an order-level contribution and break-even model once you supply revenue per order, food, packaging and other variable costs, delivery share and commission, monthly fixed costs, and operating days - then you can test whether achievable volume covers fixed costs. That still is not a guarantee.

sections.title: How to get an exact rent figure

items.text: Shortlist 3-5 named units in Dubai and 2-3 in Abu Dhabi in districts where your core categories are listed, e.g. Al Barsha, Deira, Dubai Marina, Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiyah, Al Danah, Al Manhal (evidence shows listed addresses in these areas, not that a suitable unit is available).

Request written quotations from landlords/agents per unit: annual rent, service charges, marketing fees, fit-out contribution, deposit, lease term, escalation, and permitted use. Compare all-in annual cost, not headline rent.
Then supply the eight economics inputs and I can compute contribution margin and break-even orders per month and per day; rent from a real quotation becomes part of monthly fixed costs.

assumptions: Profile: Jordanian origin; core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches; target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi; startup budget, monthly rent budget, branch format, target audience, positioning and opening date are all unset.
No rent or profit claims here are verified market facts; any rent figures you later supply are user-provided, and unit listings only show a business lists that address.

Provide the eight unit-economics inputs (revenue per order, food, packaging, other variable cost, delivery share, commission rate, monthly fixed costs, operating days) so I can run the contribution and break-even calculation.

Within what practical limit can you share unit-economics inputs - or should I first draft a cost-input checklist for you to fill from supplier and landlord quotes?
